LESSON: CONTROLLING SOIL POLLUTION

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: AGRICULTURE
Strand: Conservation of Resources
Topic 1.1: Controlling Soil Pollution

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Controlling Soil Pollution. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How can household practises cause soil pollution?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. explain the causes of soil pollution in gardening

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: CONTROLLING SOIL POLLUTION
Subject: AGRICULTURE · Grade: Grade 7
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Controlling Soil Pollution helps you succeed in AGRICULTURE. You will understand it, practise it, and use it in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

KEY FACTS: CONTROLLING SOIL POLLUTION
Controlling Soil Pollution is part of Science learning. Connect every idea to something you can observe.
Use safe examples only. Do not try dangerous experiments without a teacher.
Write definitions in your own words, then add one drawing or real-life example.

PART 1: Explain the causes of soil pollution in gardening

What this means
In this part you learn to explain the causes of soil pollution in gardening. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: explain the causes of soil pollution in gardening.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Observe: Name what you can see/touch about “Controlling Soil Pollution” around your school.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can explain the causes of soil pollution in gardening. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Controlling Soil Pollution is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Name what you can see/touch about “Controlling Soil Pollution” around your school. (skill: explain the causes of soil pollution in gardening)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Controlling Soil Pollution to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: explain the causes of soil pollution in gardening.
3. Make one local Kenya example of Controlling Soil Pollution from your county, market, farm, or school.
4. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Controlling Soil Pollution: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 7 learner study Controlling Soil Pollution?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How can household practises cause soil pollution?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Controlling Soil Pollution means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: explain the causes of soil pollution in gardening.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
